newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher, lifted by bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher, lifted by bond issues.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose sharply Tuesday, spurred by well received peso and dollar bond issues, traders said.

"The market was sustained by the Bontes auction," said a trader at a large foreign bank. Argentina auctioned $500 million of two-year Bontes treasury bonds at par for a yield of 8.0 percent Tuesday afternoon in the local market.

Peso bonds outperformed, with the government's announcement late Monday of the placing of a two-year peso bond being well received by players. The peso-denominated Bocon Previsional 1 due 2001 rose 0.85 pesos to 118.10.
The government placed 250 million pesos of two-year bonds in the international markets at par for a yield of 8.75 percent Monday.
Because the peso issue came as a surprise it served to boost the peso sector of the market more than the Bonte did for dollar bonds.
The peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 rose 0.7 pesos to 95.40, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.20 to 122.70. Argentina's FRB rose 1/4 to 86-1/4.
"The government is enjoying the current high international high liquidity levels by issuing bonds," said an analyst.

"Argentina is making the most of retail demand by issuing when and where they see demand...And why not? The success of such retail issues highlights the value of Bocons," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in an investor note.

However, market attention may turn back to focus on the root of the current strong market mood on Wednesday, namely the low yield in the U.S. Treasury market. The United States releases November producer price figures on Wednesday followed by consumer prices on Thursday and the Argentine market is expected to follow track the reaction of U.S. bonds to the indicators, said traders.
In the money markets, call money rates were unchanged at 6.38 percent.
